previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of orthotopic liver transplant, alcoholic cirrhosis, cervical spine fusion, and chronic malnutrition, was admitted for persistent nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. He was found to have a creatinine elevation likely due to dehydration, a positive urine culture for Group B Streptococcus treated with antibiotics, and a newly identified oropharyngeal fistula eroding from cervical spine hardware into the esophagus, likely exacerbated by sirolimus-induced poor wound healing. Due to the high surgical risk, he was transitioned from sirolimus to mycophenolate and prednisone and received a CT-guided GJ tube for long-term enteral nutrition. He also experienced transient sinus bradycardia attributed to ondansetron, which resolved after discontinuation. His left lower quadrant pain was due to fecal impaction, managed with suppositories. He improved with TPN and tube feeds, regained strength, and was discharged home with the GJ tube, new immunosuppression, and follow-up plans with multiple specialties.
problems: Oropharyngeal fistula with anterior cervical hardware
